leads.title: Curaçao Criminal Code (Wetboek van Strafrecht / Kódigo Penal), enacted 2011
leads.documents: Prohibits unfair discrimination and incitement to hatred and violence on grounds including 'heterosexual or homosexual orientation'; defines discrimination and penalties. Relevant as primary anti-discrimination enforcement machinery, but text cites only sexual orientation, not gender identity.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt. Cited as Article 1:221 definition of discrimination, Articles 2:61 and 2:62 penalties from fines to one year imprisonment.

leads.title: Supreme Court of the Netherlands ruling of 12 July 2024
leads.documents: Legalizes same-sex marriage in Curaçao; upholds Appeals Court decision barring discrimination based on sexual orientation.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt. Date cited: 12 July 2024.

leads.title: Appeals Court decision on same-sex marriage / sexual orientation discrimination (upheld 12 July 2024)
leads.documents: Prior appellate ruling that barring same-sex marriage is discrimination based on sexual orientation; basis for Supreme Court affirmance.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt. Referenced only as 'Appeals Court decision barring discrimination based on sexual orientation'.

leads.title: Kingdom of the Netherlands recognition requirement
leads.documents: Documents that as part of Kingdom of the Netherlands, Curaçao must recognize same-sex marriages registered in the Netherlands and in Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba as valid, even before local marriage was allowed.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt. In-text statement of Kingdom law obligation; no civil unions or other local recognition available at that time.

leads.title: April 2015 agreement of representatives of all four constituent countries
leads.documents: Political agreement that same-sex couples should have equal rights throughout the Kingdom.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt. Date cited: April 2015.

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - Oliari and Others v. Italy, August 2015
leads.documents: ECHR ruling that providing no legal recognition to same-sex couples is discriminatory; article states ECHR has jurisprudence over Curaçao.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt. Date cited: August 2015.

leads.title: 2017 proposal to the Estates of Curaçao for limited rights for same-sex couples
leads.documents: Legislative attempt to grant same-sex couples some limited rights.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt. Date cited: 2017; introduced to the Estates of Curaçao.

leads.title: 2018-2019 marriage equality bill by FOKO Curaçao, Equality Curaçao and Curaçao Gay Pro
leads.documents: Citizen-drafted bill to allow same-sex couples to marry in Curaçao; handed to Vice President of Parliament Giselle McWilliam in September 2018 during Curaçao Gay Pride, submitted to Estates 4 June 2019, withdrawn September 2020 for lack of support.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt. Key dates: handed over September 2018 sixth edition Curaçao Gay Pride; submitted 4 June 2019; withdrawn September 2020. McWilliam and Prime Minister Eugene Rhuggenaath quotes included.

leads.title: Prime Minister Eugene Rhuggenaath public statements September 2017 and September 2018
leads.documents: Government acknowledgement of LGBT discrimination/human rights issue; September 2017 'historical' speech calling for more acceptance at Willemstad Gay Pride parade; 2018 statement that 'Exclusion and discrimination against the LGBT community affects human rights' and time to debate marriage.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt. Events: Gay Pride parade Willemstad September 2017 and September 2018.
